title: Demographic and baseline characteristics of included participants
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Knowing the age and sex of participants helps you judge which patients this research describes. The population profile provides context for judging whether later findings apply to another clinical setting.

title: Analysis population and histopathological reference diagnosis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Fair diagnostic comparisons need the same participants and the same histopathological reference diagnosis. The included, excluded and reference-positive/negative counts show which records support the comparison.

title: Diagnostic classifications for MAS, hsCRP and exploratory models
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Counting correct and incorrect classifications shows what happens at each declared diagnostic threshold. TP and FN describe confirmed disease; TN and FP describe its absence. Equal totals need not mean identical participant predictions.

title: Sensitivity, specificity and accuracy of the diagnostic approaches
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: A useful diagnostic approach must identify appendicitis while also recognising its absence against histopathology. Together, sensitivity, specificity and their uncertainty describe the balance between identifying disease and recognising its absence.

title: Predictive values and likelihood ratios of the diagnostic approaches
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Predictive values and likelihood ratios connect a positive or negative test result to diagnostic uncertainty. PPV and NPV describe this cohort; likelihood ratios describe how results change prior odds. Their intervals express estimation uncertainty.

title: Discrimination of MAS and the exploratory MAS plus hsCRP model
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Discrimination asks whether a score ranks confirmed cases above reference-negative cases across thresholds. AUC summarises ranking, with its interval and evaluation method indicating the precision and context of that assessment.

title: Apparent and held-out model performance and calibration summaries
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Comparing apparent and held-out prediction performance helps reveal how a fitted model behaves beyond its own training observations. Lower Brier score or log loss indicates better probability performance in the displayed evaluation; this differs from ranking by AUC.

title: Paired comparisons of the fixed recorded diagnostic markers
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Comparing markers on the same participants preserves the paired study design. DeLong addresses raw-marker ranking; stratified McNemar addresses discordant fixed classifications. They address different aspects of paired diagnostic performance.

title: ROC curves for MAS, hsCRP and exploratory diagnostic models
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: ROC curves make the trade-off between detecting disease and false-positive results visible as thresholds change. A curve’s shape shows ranking across thresholds; the declared operating-point table explains actual binary decisions.

title: AUC estimates with conditional 95% intervals
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Plotting AUC with intervals shows both diagnostic ranking and its uncertainty in one view. Point estimates show the diagnostic ranking, while interval widths show its precision.

title: Confusion matrices for the diagnostic approaches
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: A confusion-matrix picture locates the correct decisions and the two kinds of diagnostic error. The cell counts identify the denominators behind sensitivity, specificity and predictive values.

title: Held-out calibration of exploratory diagnostic models
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Calibration plots compare predicted probabilities with observed disease proportions. Agreement with the diagonal supports probability agreement within the plotted bins; inspect each bin’s size and interval.

title: hsCRP distribution by histological appendicitis severity
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Describing hs-CRP separately in simple and complicated histology reveals the measurements behind the severity question. Medians, spread and group sizes help you see variability before considering a diagnostic threshold.

title: Comparison of hsCRP between simple and complicated appendicitis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The severity comparison asks whether recorded hs-CRP differs between the defined simple and complicated groups. The difference, its interval and the test result distinguish effect magnitude from statistical evidence.

title: Discrimination of complicated histology by continuous hsCRP
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This analysis asks how hs-CRP distinguishes complicated from simple confirmed appendicitis. The positive target here is complicated histology, not appendicitis versus its absence; interpret the denominators accordingly.

title: Distribution of hsCRP in simple and complicated appendicitis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The box plot makes the spread and overlap of hs-CRP in simple and complicated histology easy to inspect. The medians and boxes show typical values and variability; the adjacent test provides evidence beyond the visual pattern.

title: ROC curve of hsCRP for complicated histological appendicitis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This ROC curve shows the trade-off when hs-CRP ranks complicated rather than simple confirmed appendicitis. The curve and companion AUC interval describe severity discrimination across thresholds.

title: Reference diagnosis and analysis population by predefined age group
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Subgroup denominators show how much evidence is available for children under 16 and adults aged 16 or above. The reference-positive and negative counts explain why subgroup estimates may differ in precision.

title: Performance of the pooled MAS plus hsCRP model by age group
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The age analysis checks the same pooled combined model within the predefined child and adult groups. Separate subgroup denominators and intervals show how precisely sensitivity and specificity are estimated.

title: Reliable between-age-group comparison of model AUC
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This planned output addresses reliable between-age-group comparison of model AUC. Only one reference-negative child is present in the supplied cohort. Reliable paediatric AUC uncertainty and between-group comparison cannot be established; more independent reference-negative children are required.

title: Descriptive age-specific ROC curves for the pooled combined model
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Separate age-group ROC curves make subgroup ranking patterns visible for the pooled combined model. Reference counts indicate how much evidence supports each subgroup curve.

title: Age-specific sensitivity and specificity with 95% intervals
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Displaying age-specific sensitivity and specificity together highlights which type of diagnostic performance is supported in each group. Wide intervals signal limited precision even when a point estimate appears high.

title: Detailed histopathological diagnoses in the specimen-linked operated cohort
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Detailed pathology frequencies explain which diagnoses underlie the final disease-status classification. Keep confirmed inflammation separate from isolated reactive lymphoid hyperplasia and unknown findings.

title: Proportion negative for acute appendicitis in the operated cohort
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The negative appendicectomy estimate describes operated specimens without confirmed acute appendicitis under the operational definition. The denominator and interval describe the frequency and precision of this outcome.

title: Negative reference diagnosis by age group and sex
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This comparison asks whether reference-negative proportions differ across the recorded age and sex groups. Subgroup denominators and Fisher’s exact results distinguish observed proportions from evidence of a group difference.

title: Distribution of specimens across detailed histopathological diagnoses
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The bars show how operated specimens are distributed across the original histopathology labels. The heights reveal which diagnoses contribute most to the cohort’s reference-status distribution.

title: Diagnostic-confidence ratings before and after MAS and hsCRP information
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Before-and-after confidence distributions describe how clinicians rated certainty for complete paired cases. The five ordered categories describe reported certainty without assuming equally spaced numerical measurements.

title: Paired transitions in diagnostic-confidence ratings
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The transition table preserves each case’s before-and-after rating rather than comparing unrelated totals. Cells above or below the unchanged diagonal identify the direction of movement between ordered ratings.

title: Direction of paired diagnostic-confidence change
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Counting increased, unchanged and decreased ratings gives a simple overview of paired confidence movement. The direction of change is meaningful without assuming equal distances between Likert categories.

title: Inferential comparison of paired diagnostic confidence
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This planned output addresses inferential comparison of paired diagnostic confidence. Same clinician within each patient pair is confirmed, but clinician identifiers and repeated-case linkage are unavailable. An independent-pair Wilcoxon p-value or a clinician-clustered alternative cannot be justified without that structure.

title: Comparison between resident doctors and medical officers
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This planned output addresses comparison between resident doctors and medical officers. The SAV has neither professional-group assignment nor clinician identifiers, and no direct ease-of-diagnosis item. Confidence cannot be relabelled as ease or used to invent these groups.

title: Paired diagnostic-confidence transitions before and after information
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The heatmap makes common before-and-after confidence transitions visible while retaining the paired structure. Movement away from the diagonal shows changes between ordered ratings.

title: Before and after diagnostic-confidence rating distributions
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Side-by-side rating distributions show how the overall confidence profile changes among complete pairs. The accompanying transition output distinguishes individual changes that marginal bars cannot reveal.

title: Recorded total hospital expenditure in the study cohort
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The expenditure summary describes the recorded financial burden in this cohort in NGN. Typical costs and their spread show whether an average alone adequately represents the observed amounts.

title: Incremental direct hospital cost of adding hsCRP to MAS
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This planned output addresses incremental direct hospital cost of adding hsCRP to MAS. Itemised hsCRP costs, resource quantities/unit prices and a comparable routine diagnostic pathway are absent. Recorded total costs alone cannot estimate incremental cost, savings or cost-effectiveness.

title: Distribution of recorded total hospital expenditure
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The histogram shows how recorded total hospital expenditure is distributed rather than hiding its shape in one average. Concentration, skew and high-cost tails help explain why mean and median may differ.

title: Recorded hospital costs by histological appendicitis severity
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Cost summaries by histological severity describe the recorded expenditure behind the simple-versus-complicated comparison. Typical costs, variation and group sizes provide the descriptive context for the financial comparison.

title: Hospital-cost differences between simple and complicated appendicitis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The cost comparison evaluates the magnitude and statistical evidence for differences between the severity groups. Complicated-minus-simple effects and intervals in NGN quantify the financial difference alongside the rank or Welch result.

title: Adjusted hospital-cost association estimates
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This planned output addresses adjusted hospital-cost association estimates. No approved adjustment set or itemised cost-driver measurements were supplied; only eight complicated cases are present. An automatic multivariable cost-driver model would be unsupported.

title: Recorded hospital costs in simple and complicated histological appendicitis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The box plot shows how recorded hospital costs vary and overlap between simple and complicated histology. Median and spread reveal features hidden by a single group average; the adjacent test informs the comparison.

title: Common analysis population for AIR, MAS, hsCRP and combined models
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Fair diagnostic comparisons need the same participants and the same histopathological reference diagnosis. The included, excluded and reference-positive/negative counts show which records support the comparison.

heading: Essence and Practical Importance

heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Comparing apparent and held-out prediction performance helps reveal how a fitted model behaves beyond its own training observations. Lower Brier score or log loss indicates better probability performance in the displayed evaluation; this differs from ranking by AUC.

title: Classification confusion matrices across strategies
heading: Essence and Practical Importance

title: Held-out calibration plots for exploratory combined models
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Calibration plots compare predicted probabilities with observed disease proportions. Agreement with the diagonal supports probability agreement within the plotted bins; inspect each bin’s size and interval.

title: Exploratory score, biomarker, interval and cost associations
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The association table explores how recorded scores, biomarkers, costs and intervals vary together. Correlation direction and uncertainty indicate monotonic relationships; use the supplied Holm-adjusted p-values for this family.

title: Prespecified multivariable association or causal estimates
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This planned output addresses prespecified multivariable association or causal estimates. No approved causal adjustment set or multivariable exploratory specification is supplied. Do not automatically regress every available variable against every outcome.

title: Recorded AIR score and hsCRP association
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The scatter plot lets you inspect the actual recorded AIR–hs-CRP pairs rather than only a correlation coefficient. The plotted direction, spread and unusual pairs complement the matching Spearman result.

title: Exploratory associations with conditional 95% intervals
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The forest plot puts exploratory correlation directions and uncertainty side by side. Intervals show how precisely each relationship is estimated; the companion table carries multiplicity-aware evidence.

title: Distribution of recorded AIR scores and working risk categories
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The AIR distribution summarises the recorded measurements and their assigned reference or risk categories. Continuous values in points and category denominators show the variation concealed by grouped categories.

title: Comparison of AIR scores by histopathological reference diagnosis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This comparison asks whether recorded AIR differs between histopathology-positive and negative specimens. Group sizes, effect magnitude, uncertainty and the test result together describe the strength and precision of the comparison.

title: Association of AIR risk categories with histopathological diagnosis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The category cross-tabulation asks how AIR categories are distributed across histopathological disease status. Category counts, the exact test and association effect provide the denominators and evidence needed to assess the relationship.

title: Association of AIR risk categories with histological severity
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This cross-tabulation asks how the working AIR risk groups relate to simple and complicated histology. Category counts and the exact association test show whether the distribution differs, not whether AIR determines severity.

title: Diagnostic performance of continuous AIR and its working high-risk threshold
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This output evaluates recorded AIR against histopathology using continuous ranking and a working high-risk threshold. Distinguish the AUC question from the sensitivity/specificity at the declared score cutoff.

title: Exploratory AIR associations with costs and recorded hospital intervals
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: These correlations examine how recorded AIR varies with the other listed scores, costs or hospital intervals. Each named pair’s direction, interval, sample size and supplied adjustment describe its association and uncertainty.

title: Distribution of recorded AIR scores
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The histogram shows the shape and concentration of recorded AIR measurements in points. A distribution shows spread and tails that a single average cannot communicate.

title: Participants in the working AIR risk categories
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The category bars show how many participants fall into the working AIR risk bands. Category definitions and counts identify the comparisons represented by the disease-status outcomes.

title: ROC curve for continuous AIR against histopathology
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The AIR ROC curve shows its ranking of reference-positive versus negative specimens across score thresholds. The companion AUC interval and threshold-specific rates describe the diagnostic trade-off.

title: AIR scores by histopathological reference diagnosis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The box plot makes the spread and overlap of AIR in reference-positive and negative specimens visible. Plotted medians and spread complement the matching statistical comparison.

title: Recorded AIR scores by postoperative-complication status
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The postoperative comparison asks whether recorded AIR differs between documented complication and explicit no-complication groups. Actual group counts and the test result provide context for the observed difference.

title: Distribution of PCV and external reference categories
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The PCV distribution summarises the recorded measurements and their assigned reference or risk categories. Continuous values in % and category denominators show the variation concealed by grouped categories.

title: Age- and sex-specific PCV reference intervals used in classification
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The reference table makes the age- and sex-specific PCV boundaries used for classification transparent. Checking these limits helps distinguish a measured percentage from an externally assigned low, normal or high category.

title: Comparison of PCV by histopathological reference diagnosis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This comparison asks whether recorded PCV differs between histopathology-positive and negative specimens. Group sizes, effect magnitude, uncertainty and the test result together describe the strength and precision of the comparison.

title: Comparison of PCV in simple and complicated appendicitis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This comparison asks whether PCV differs between the defined simple and complicated appendicitis groups. Effect magnitude, group sizes and the test result distinguish an observed difference from the evidence supporting it.

title: Association of PCV category with histopathological diagnosis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The category cross-tabulation asks how PCV categories are distributed across histopathological disease status. Category counts, the exact test and association effect provide the denominators and evidence needed to assess the relationship.

title: Association of PCV category with working AIR risk category
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The cross-tabulation compares external PCV categories with working AIR risk categories. The exact test and association effect describe category alignment, rather than proving the scores measure the same process.

title: Exploratory PCV associations with AIR, costs and hospital stay
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: These correlations examine how recorded PCV varies with the other listed scores, costs or hospital intervals. Each named pair’s direction, interval, sample size and supplied adjustment describe its association and uncertainty.

title: Distribution of recorded PCV
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The histogram shows the shape and concentration of recorded PCV measurements in %. A distribution shows spread and tails that a single average cannot communicate.

title: PCV by histopathological reference diagnosis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The box plot makes the spread and overlap of PCV in reference-positive and negative specimens visible. Plotted medians and spread complement the matching statistical comparison.

title: Recorded PCV and AIR score
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The scatter plot shows paired recorded PCV percentages and AIR scores. The pattern and matching Spearman result help distinguish a directional relationship from scattered variation.

title: Recorded PCV by postoperative-complication status
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The postoperative comparison asks whether recorded PCV differs between documented complication and explicit no-complication groups. Actual group counts and the test result provide context for the observed difference.

title: Documented presence, absence and unknown status of clinical signs
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The sign inventory distinguishes documented presence, explicit absence and unknown status. A selected sign in a single-choice field supplies a documented positive, not proof that every other sign was absent.

title: Recorded clinical signs by histopathological reference diagnosis
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The sign cross-tabulation asks how documented findings are distributed across reference-positive and negative histology. Each finding’s group counts, exact-test evidence and recording rules define the scope of its comparison.

title: Recorded clinical signs by histological severity
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The sign cross-tabulation asks how documented findings are distributed across simple and complicated histology. Each finding’s group counts, exact-test evidence and recording rules define the scope of its comparison.

title: Recorded clinical signs across working AIR risk categories
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The sign cross-tabulation asks how documented findings are distributed across working AIR categories. Each finding’s group counts, exact-test evidence and recording rules define the scope of its comparison.

title: Diagnostic rates of fully documented binary signs
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Diagnostic rates show how fully recorded binary signs agree with histopathological disease status. Sensitivity and specificity require explicit recorded absence as well as presence; inspect each sign’s denominator.

title: Classification counts and likelihood ratios of documented binary signs
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: Classification counts and likelihood ratios show how a documented binary sign changes diagnostic odds. Check the true/false counts and uncertainty rather than treating a present sign as diagnostic proof.

title: Documented clinical-sign presence among study participants
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The sign bars show documented presence across recorded fields. Distinguish positive-only selected-sign counts from prevalence based on complete Yes/No recording.

title: Sensitivity and specificity of confirmed binary clinical signs
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: The rate plot compares sensitivity and specificity for explicitly documented binary signs. Intervals and sign-specific denominators reveal precision alongside the point estimates.

title: Incremental value of clinical signs added to existing scores
heading: Essence and Practical Importance
text: This planned output addresses incremental value of clinical signs added to existing scores. MAS and AIR already incorporate overlapping signs. No justified nonredundant predictor specification, complete sign absences or adequate rare-reference sample for further model development has been supplied.
